summary: Command-line browser automation for AI agents that drives your own logged-in Chrome, with ready adapters that turn websites into commands.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: OpenCLI is a browser automation CLI for people and AI agents. It can navigate, inspect, click, fill forms, extract and screenshot pages in your real Chrome session, and built-in adapters turn sites like Reddit, Hacker News and Twitter/X into repeatable commands.
sixtySeconds.problem: Agents that use a fresh headless browser get blocked by logins. OpenCLI works through your existing Chrome profile so the agent sees what you see.
whoFor: Developers giving coding agents a browser
People automating sites they are logged in to
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for deterministic site commands plus general browser control from one CLI, with a skill for agents like Claude Code and Cursor.

overview: Setup has three parts: install OpenCLI (the OpenCLIApp desktop app on macOS and Windows, or the npm package), install the Browser Bridge extension in Chrome, and run opencli doctor to check the connection. A small local daemon starts automatically.
Use built-in adapters for supported sites, use opencli browser commands to operate any page, or write new adapters with the adapter tools.
AI agents can use it through the opencli-browser skill. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
